PullRequest.Title: editor: stabilize Connected tab multi-selection styling
PullRequest.Body:

Connected multi-selected editor tabs now use consistent selected surfaces and visible selection accents instead of mixing short selected pills with a differently framed active tab. Modified-file highlighting and high-contrast focus remain distinct from selection.

Related to #341150.

- Keep the active tab connected to the editor without coloring the entire document frame as a selection.
- Preserve a thin selection accent with **Highlight Modified Tabs** off; with it on, modified files use their theme's stronger accent without covering selection boundaries.
- Preserve high-contrast selection/focus outlines and clear stale modified accents when the next theme or active state supplies no modified color.
- Keep ordinary unselected-tab hover behavior unchanged, and avoid doubling the accent on selected tabs in the bottom wrapped row.

### Visuals

Native Windows Code OSS. These are settled appearance states reached through real tab interactions, not interaction recordings or before/after captures.

**Modified highlighting, Dark 2026:** all three tabs are selected, `geometry.ts` is active and modified, and its Close action is hovered.

**Modified highlighting off:** each selected tab has the same thin selection line.

![Connected multi-selection with modified highlighting off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4ddca33-a9be-460a-931c-3988e3b462d3)

**Modified highlighting on:** `geometry.ts` has the stronger modified-file accent; its clean selected neighbors retain the thin selection line.

![Connected multi-selection with modified highlighting on](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b3f7c51-493c-4c44-a001-3895ff98c501)

**Default High Contrast:** the modified active tab clears the inactive modified accent and retains the selected outline, including beside Close.

![High Contrast multi-selection with the modified tab active and Close hovered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfb60dd4-1079-4def-a0a4-3ba66d4bd1be)

**Broader layout preservation:** all 29 Light editor-tab fixture screenshots were inspected in the [completed CI screenshot report](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/41128464258). They cover compact/default density, upper/bottom wrapped rows, pinned icon-only/separate rows, scrolling, long-name sizing, file icons, breadcrumbs, hidden/leading/unreserved Close actions, and Connected/Pill/Legacy styles. These are fixture renders of the CI merge containing `e6f7644`, not native interaction captures.

**Light fixture example:** selected inactive tabs use full-height surfaces and thin top accents alongside the active tab. File-status decorations and unselected tabs remain distinct.

![Light CI fixture: modified and multi-selected Connected editor tabs](https://hediet-screenshots.azurewebsites.net/images/4c12be35d49df8335b1357fee35477f2efd6940c228ef47218e67734e677a927)

### Try it

1. Enable Modern UI and Connected editor tabs. Open three or more files and modify one without saving.
2. Select one tab, then Ctrl-click a second. Both selected tabs should retain their top selection accent. Select more tabs with Ctrl-click or Shift-click, then switch the active selected tab. Hover an inactive selected tab and its Close action: the tab surface should not grow.
3. Toggle `workbench.editor.highlightModifiedTabs` off and on. Selection stays visible in both states; only the modified file gains the stronger accent when the theme supplies one.
4. Repeat in Default High Contrast with the modified tab inactive, then active. Its inactive white modified accent must not persist when it becomes active or when the theme changes.
5. Enable wrapping and narrow the editor group until selected tabs occupy the bottom row. Their clean and modified accents should retain their normal thickness rather than gaining an extra line.

### Validation

- Manually validated by Cherry through remote desktop.
- Fifty native appearance states checked across Dark 2026, Light 2026, Default High Contrast and Default High Contrast Light, with modified highlighting off/on. Real plain/Ctrl/Shift selection and Close-hover states checked; PNG pixel assertions verify accent presence and thickness.
- Four additional native Dark 2026 states checked on `e6f7644`: clean/modified single selection, two selected tabs, and inactive modified-tab Close hover. Selected surfaces retained equal height.
- The broader native keyboard-focus, wrapped multi-selection, pinned/overflow interaction and high-zoom matrix was not completed. The layout evidence above is static CI coverage, supplemented by the targeted browser/Electron tests below; it does not establish those native interactions.
- `npm run compile` — passed.
- `node build\lib\preLaunch.ts` — passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed for the final follow-up.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\test\browser\parts\editor\multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` — passed; the unchanged production TypeScript also passed its earlier targeted lint.
- `npm run stylelint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\modernUI\browser\media\connectedEditorTabs.css` — passed.
- With `CI=1`, `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\test\browser\parts\editor\multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\test\browser\editorPart.test.ts --grep "single-row Connected selected and modified inactive fills|wrapped bottom-row selection accents|Connected panel rows match panel header height across hosts|regular-theme Connected multi-selection" --reporter dot --timeout 120000` — four passed, covering selected/modified geometry, wrapped accents and ordinary cross-host hover behavior.
- Headless Chromium unit runner — twelve passed across the same two files, including high-contrast, modified/off-on, theme transitions and action-overlay coverage.
- New stale-accent regression failed before the production cleanup and passed afterward.
- [CI for `e6f7644`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/41128464455) — compile/hygiene, all six platform browser/Electron UI unit jobs, smoke/integration tests and the PR gate passed. [Screenshots and fixture tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/41128464258) also passed. The remaining **VS Code PR Check** requires one collaborator approval; it is not a failing test.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting multiple Connected editor tabs or switching the active tab
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selection event synchronously reaches editorGroupView.onDidChangeEditorSelection, MultiEditorTabsControl.updateEditorSelections, and the existing per-tab redraw/layout path before the tab strip visually settles. The diff changes only CSS matching for selected/multi-selected tab surfaces; it adds no new JavaScript loop or geometry read.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The existing redraw scales with the number of open tabs in the affected editor group. New selector dependencies apply only to local .tab-fill or .tab-connected-edge descendants of selected tabs, so effective cardinality is the rendered tabs in that group, not the whole workbench.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM class updates, style resolution, and painting are serialized on the renderer UI thread; there is no queue, worker, or concurrent external operation introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stylesheet is already eagerly loaded by the Modern UI contribution and browser selector matching is reused under normal style-engine behavior. No application cache, cache key, miss path, coalescing, or negative cache is added or changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous renderer path and group-local cardinality from the traced callers and selectors; there is no evidence of a materially larger invalidation scope or added forced layout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-recalculation duration depends on tab count, theme, wrapping, and browser state, but the added rules use explicit class/pseudo-class dependencies local to tab descendants and avoid the repository's documented high-risk :has and class-substring patterns.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds visual style rules on an already synchronous tab redraw path but does not introduce forced geometry reads, extra relayout calls, broad invalidation hazards, or meaningful repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dirty-tab updates, theme changes, and toggling modified-tab highlighting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A dirty-state event synchronously redraws the affected tab; selection/group/theme/options redraws may visit existing tabs. The added else branch removes a stale class and custom property when a dirty highlighted tab has no resolved modified color, before the existing active/selection styling and layout complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A direct dirty event affects one tab. Existing selection/group-wide redraws scale with open tabs, while the new cleanup executes only for dirty tabs with highlighting enabled and no resolved modified color; standard light/dark themes define these colors, narrowing the realistic affected set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer DOM mutations execute serially on the UI thread. No asynchronous task, limiter, burst, or backpressure behavior changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme color lookup behavior is unchanged. The branch clears DOM state rather than retaining or introducing cached data; there are no cache keys, cold/warm fetches, or coalescing concerns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and bounded mutation count; low evidence for any measurable degradation, so no finding is warranted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The branch can issue two idempotent DOM API calls in uncommon no-color theme states, but there is no evidence that absent-value removals trigger material style/layout work or that this path is frequent enough for user-visible cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The cleanup is bounded, does not add geometry reads or external work, and prevents retained stale styling state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hovering/focusing Connected tabs and rendering wrapped bottom rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser pseudo-class or class changes cause style resolution and repaint for tab fill/accent rules on the interaction critical path. The changed CSS preserves geometry for selected/dirty tabs and paints gradients/borders; it does not invoke script, synchronous measurement, or a new layout routine.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Matching is bounded by rendered tabs in the active editor group and primarily by the hovered/focused/selected elements and their immediate surface descendants. Wrapped rows do not create additional DOM items beyond existing tabs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Style calculation, layout if needed, and paint are browser-renderer work serialized on the UI thread; no independent expensive operations are launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Static CSS rules have no application-managed cache behavior. Cold startup parses a few additional rules once; subsequent interactions use the loaded stylesheet, with no changed invalidation cache contract.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the rules are local and avoid known hazardous selector forms; no concrete performance mechanism meeting the reporting threshold was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Paint cost varies with zoom and selected-tab count, but the added gradients and borders are constant-complexity per visible selected tab and provide no evidence of dropped frames or broad workbench invalidation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The rendering changes are constant-complexity per visible tab and do not add a proven layout, rendering, or style-invalidation hazard.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff page. Traced selection, active/dirty redraw, theme/options transitions, hover/focus, wrapping, stylesheet loading, and renderer layout paths. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression or concrete regression fix was established.
